# Task-complete forward data and finite passive control certificates

15 October 2026. Base b7cada92d2eb304578be5ed974f1e44b10a89928. Root derivation, initially independent of parallel workers. These are exact mathematical statements about declared static linear systems. Matrix identities, linear identification and passivity are established machinery; historical originality is UNKNOWN. No physical implementation, equally informed advantage or dynamic-stability certificate follows.

## 1. An unrestricted hidden defect can leave the task gradient unbounded

Write K=A^{-1}, with real square A and strictly positive symmetric part. Then sym K=K^T(sym A)K is strictly positive. Conversely strict positivity of sym K implies K invertible and sym(K^{-1}) positive. All claims below are within this open static accretive cone, without a supplied uniform norm or coercivity bound.

Suppose the acquisition gives full response K v for all v in a measured source subspace V. Grant complete state readout, no noise and arbitrarily many repetitions. Let the nonzero objective source c belong to V, as in the incoming closure protocol. For any target tangent source q outside V, the scalar c^T K q can assume every real value while all those responses remain exactly unchanged.

Choose an orthonormal basis for V and its complement, and write

    K = [[H,Z],[G,T]].

The measured columns fix H and G. S=sym H is strictly positive. Choose any Z and set

    C=(Z+G^T)/2,
    T=C^T S^{-1} C+I.

Then sym K=[[S,C],[C^T,C^T S^{-1}C+I]] is strictly positive by square completion. Thus every Z is legal in this declared mathematical class. Since c=(c_V,0), q=(q_V,q_Q), c_V and q_Q are nonzero, choose Z so that

    c_V^T Z q_Q = t-c_V^T H q_V

for any desired t. This constructs the whole real task-response fiber, not just an opposite-sign pair. All probes in V, including b,c and the assumed nonreciprocal ports if present, are unchanged. No acquired global coercivity or operator bound may be silently held fixed during this construction: such a bound is additional information and can restrict the fiber. Only settled static responses are fixed. Transient trajectories, measured settling-time bounds and spectral information are additional acquisitions and need not agree across this family; no dynamic indistinguishability is claimed.

# Task-restricted completion and validation of a physical adjoint

Date 2026-10-15. Internal mathematical derivations and synthetic checks.
Source pin `b7cada92d2eb304578be5ed974f1e44b10a89928`. No laboratory evidence,
historical novelty or independent mathematical review is asserted.

The proposed operation is a physical use of established dot-product testing
and independent Gaussian residual validation. It can acquire task-specific
accuracy without acquiring a global nonreciprocity support certificate.
It does require additional injection access on the relevant control-force
space, and its amplitude/precision costs cannot be hidden in a profile count.

## 1. Incoming construction reconstructed

At one fixed loaded real linear operating point, write Ax=b, J=F(x,p),
c=F_x and lambda=A^{-T}c. A parameter direction d has tangent force
f_d=b'_d-A'_d x and first derivative F'_d+f_d^T lambda.

Under the supplied port hypothesis A=R+PKP^T with R symmetric, acquire
Y=A^{-1}P, z=A^{-1}c, H=P^T Y. For invertible A and H, the incoming estimate is

\[
 \alpha=H^{-1}P^Tz,\quad
 \beta=H^{-1}(H^T-H)\alpha,\quad
 \hat\lambda=z+Y\beta.                                    \tag{1}
\]

Put D0=K^T-K. Then A^T=A+P D0 P^T and the low-rank inverse identity gives
H^T=(I+H D0)^{-1}H. Inverting this identity shows
D=H^{-T}-H^{-1}=D0. Thus A^T=A+PDP^T, and (1) solves the adjoint.
The acquisition uses b, k port profiles and c, with the same A and calibrated
source/sensor loading. Only rows needed for port solves and control forces
need be stored. The interior need not be reconstructed, but the port support
premise is not supplied by this acquisition.

The exact source pair A±=I±e2 e4^T, b=e1, c=e2, P=[e3,e5], v=e1-e4 has
identical full responses to all protocol profiles. Its conductance update
has J±(p)=∓p/(1+2p), so the control decision differs. The symmetric part has
minimum eigenvalue 1/2. This falsifies support certification, not (1) under
its actual hypothesis. The source empirical trace reanalysis concerns an
established reciprocal baseline, not an experiment on (1).

# An acquired load-control quotient instead of a completed adjoint

Date: 15 October 2026. Status: internally derived, not externally reviewed; historical novelty UNKNOWN. No new experiment or technological advantage is claimed. This note reconstructs a task-sufficient part of existing Virtual VNA machinery, with an explicit rectangular observation contract and exact finite-load recovery. The primary source itself already contains the diagonal scaling equivalence; the broader operation of learning a compact tunable-wave model is established prior art.

## 1. Exact target and acquired inputs

At one fixed frequency or in a real static linear regime, suppose an unknown fixed plant belongs to the family

    A(q) = A0 + V diag(q) V^T,
    M(q) = C^T A(q)^(-1) B,                         (1)

where A0 is invertible, V has m columns, B has a source columns, and C has b readout columns. Matrices may be complex; T is the algebraic transpose in this network formula, not the Hermitian adjoint. There is no reciprocity assumption on A0. The state dimension may be arbitrarily larger than m,a,b.

The accessible measurement is the coherent b-by-a transfer block M(q). Its columns require a linearly independent settled source profiles at each load setting. The controls are calibrated scalar load increments q_i relative to a common reference q=0. The physically chosen B,C and their gains must stay the same throughout. The unknown local state fields and V need not be numerically supplied to the estimator, but the physical loading law (1) must be independently justified. A single lumped element or a qualified conductance edge is a possible realization. Arbitrary changes of unknown components do not automatically satisfy (1).

We target only decisions whose outputs depend on M(q), including a fixed accessible input u, a measured output M(q)u, and a known objective F(M(q)u,q). We do not target hidden state fields, unknown component derivatives, or a full physical adjoint. This target matches finite load-setting decisions even if all nonreciprocity is distributed throughout the hidden plant.

For a real strictly accretive A0 and real V, every q>=0 preserves strict accretivity, hence invertibility. This supplies an algebraic safe set under a justified premise; it is not an experimental certification of that premise or a dynamical stability proof. Complex frequency-domain admissible
